title: Neurons: Structure, Types and Myelin Sheath
summary: Neuron structure and function; types of neurons; myelin sheath; action potential; phases of action potential; refractory periods.
objectives: Distinguish sensory, motor and interneuron types.
revision: Neuron = dendrites → soma → axon → axon terminals. Myelin sheath insulates and speeds conduction. Action potential: depolarisation → repolarisation → refractory.
traps: Myelin sheath speeds conduction via saltatory propagation at nodes of Ranvier.
confusions: Believing myelin sheath generates action potentials.

notes.t: A neuron is the basic working unit of the brain and nervous system — a specialised cell that transmits information to other nerve cells, muscle or gland cells.

notes.c: Parts of a neuron and their functions
r: Contains the nucleus and maintains the cell.
Carries the neural impulse away from the cell body.
Insulating layer that speeds up impulse transmission.
Gaps in myelin sheath that speed conduction.
Carry signals from receptors to CNS
Carry signals from CNS to muscles/glands

notes.t: An action potential is a rapid rise and fall in membrane potential that travels down the axon. Phases: depolarisation, repolarisation, hyperpolarisation and refractory periods.

Worked example: Resting potential is approximately -70 mV. During depolarisation, voltage-gated sodium channels open and the membrane potential rises to about +30 mV. During repolarisation, potassium channels open and the potential returns toward -70 mV.
Neuron structure, myelin sheath function and action potential phases are frequently tested in UGC NET biological basis questions.
